items.stem: Under accrual accounting in US GAAP, when is revenue generally recognised?

options.text: When the performance obligation is satisfied, regardless of when cash is received
options.rationale: Correct: accrual accounting ties recognition to satisfying obligations, not cash timing.
That describes cash-basis accounting, not accrual.

options.text: At the end of the fiscal year only
options.rationale: Recognition follows the obligation, not a fixed calendar point.
Signing alone does not satisfy a performance obligation.

items.explanation: Correct: accrual accounting ties recognition to satisfying obligations, not cash timing.

items.stem: Which TWO are steps in the ASC 606 five-step revenue recognition model?

options.text: Identify the contract with a customer
options.rationale: Correct: identifying the contract is the first step.

options.text: Allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations
options.rationale: Correct: price allocation is a core step of the model.
Depreciation is not part of the revenue model.
Dividends are unrelated to revenue recognition steps.

options.text: Revalue inventory to market each period
options.rationale: Inventory measurement is separate from the revenue steps.

items.explanation: Correct: identifying the contract is the first step.

items.stem: Why should a qualifying expenditure on a long-lived asset be capitalised rather than expensed?

options.text: Because the asset provides benefits over multiple periods, matching cost to those periods
options.rationale: Correct: capitalising and depreciating spreads the cost over the periods benefited.

options.text: Because expensing is prohibited for all purchases
options.rationale: Many costs are correctly expensed; only qualifying assets are capitalised.
Capitalising reduces, not increases, current-period expense.
This is an accrual/matching concept, not a cash-basis rule.

items.explanation: Correct: capitalising and depreciating spreads the cost over the periods benefited.
